answer: Each agent’s public identity is registered only after hardware-rooted attestation verifies its enclave runs the approved MRENCLAVE; its key is generated and protected within that trusted environment. Verifiers reject software-only replicas, so duplicating identities requires access to genuine attested SGX or SEV hardware rather than copying virtual machines. This raises the cost of Sybil attacks: an attacker must acquire physical silicon to forge a fleet. No sonnet can make cloned code wander past that hardware check.
